The student must connect the two formulas and eliminate the unknown sector fraction to find the radius, then recover the angle and sketch; the table does not scaffold that elimination.

answer.short: Area of circle: $36\pi$; area of sector: $18\pi$.
Angle: $90^\circ$; fraction: $\frac14$; circumference: $12\pi$; arc length: $3\pi$; area of circle: $36\pi$; area of sector: $9\pi$.
answer.worked:
The marked region is a quadrant.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=90^\circ\\f&=\frac{90}{360}=\frac14\\C&=2\pi(6)=12\pi\\L&=\frac14(12\pi)=3\pi\\A_{\text{circle}}&=\pi(6)^2=36\pi\\A_{\text{sector}}&=\frac14(36\pi)=9\pi\end{align*}$$

answer.short: Sketch a $45^\circ$ sector. Radius: $6$; fraction: $\frac18$; arc length: $1.5\pi$; area of circle: $36\pi$; area of sector: $4.5\pi$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}C&=2\pi r\\12\pi&=2\pi r\\r&=6\\f&=\frac{45}{360}=\frac18\\L&=\frac18(12\pi)=\frac{3\pi}{2}=1.5\pi\\A_{\text{circle}}&=\pi(6)^2=36\pi\\A_{\text{sector}}&=\frac18(36\pi)=\frac{9\pi}{2}=4.5\pi\end{align*}$$
Draw two radii $45^\circ$ apart and identify the smaller sector.

answer.short: Sketch a $60^\circ$ sector. Angle: $60^\circ$; fraction: $\frac16$; circumference: $12\pi$; area of circle: $36\pi$; area of sector: $6\pi$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}C&=2\pi(6)=12\pi\\f&=\frac{L}{C}=\frac{2\pi}{12\pi}=\frac16\\\theta&=\frac16(360^\circ)=60^\circ\\A_{\text{circle}}&=\pi(6)^2=36\pi\\A_{\text{sector}}&=\frac16(36\pi)=6\pi\end{align*}$$

answer.short: Sketch a $120^\circ$ sector. Radius: $6$; angle: $120^\circ$; fraction: $\frac13$; circumference: $12\pi$; arc length: $4\pi$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{circle}}&=\pi r^2\\36\pi&=\pi r^2\\r^2&=36\\r&=6\\f&=\frac{12\pi}{36\pi}=\frac13\\\theta&=\frac13(360^\circ)=120^\circ\\C&=2\pi(6)=12\pi\\L&=\frac13(12\pi)=4\pi\end{align*}$$
Draw two radii $120^\circ$ apart and identify the smaller sector.

answer.short: Sketch a $30^\circ$ sector. Radius: $12$; angle: $30^\circ$; fraction: $\frac1{12}$; area of circle: $144\pi$; area of sector: $12\pi$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}C&=2\pi r\\24\pi&=2\pi r\\r&=12\\f&=\frac{L}{C}=\frac{2\pi}{24\pi}=\frac1{12}\\\theta&=\frac1{12}(360^\circ)=30^\circ\\A_{\text{circle}}&=\pi(12)^2=144\pi\\A_{\text{sector}}&=\frac1{12}(144\pi)=12\pi\end{align*}$$
Draw two radii $30^\circ$ apart and identify the smaller sector.

answer.short: Sketch a quadrant. Radius: $12$; angle: $90^\circ$; fraction: $\frac14$; circumference: $24\pi$; area of circle: $144\pi$.
answer.worked:
Let $f$ be the fraction of the circle. Divide the sector-area equation by the arc-length equation to find $r$.
$$\begin{align*}L&=f(2\pi r)\\6\pi&=f(2\pi r)\\A_{\text{sector}}&=f\pi r^2\\36\pi&=f\pi r^2\\\frac{36\pi}{6\pi}&=\frac{f\pi r^2}{f(2\pi r)}\\6&=\frac r2\\r&=12\\C&=2\pi(12)=24\pi\\f&=\frac{6\pi}{24\pi}=\frac14\\\theta&=\frac14(360^\circ)=90^\circ\\A_{\text{circle}}&=\pi(12)^2=144\pi\end{align*}$$
Identify one quadrant of the circle.
